What Zelda analyzed The work behind this report — counted, not estimated. 12 Pages analyzed 12 Sections searched 2 Categories analyzed Business Model & Growth Analysis Insufficient disclosed data to describe the business model. The extracted evidence contains no revenue statement, no pricing or monetisation mechanism, no identification of the paying customer, and no statement about growth drivers or expansion plans. The only operational data are traction metrics — the company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages (measurement basis questioned; see open concerns) on a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2, S3] — which confirm product usage activity but do not establish how or whether the company monetises that activity. Information Readiness Score: 10/100 Present: • Usage/traction figures: the company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages (slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16') [S1, S2] • A second messages figure of 500M/month stated elsewhere in the deck [S3] • A funding-raised figure of $23.1M listed by Pitch Deck Hunt [S4] • Stage (Series A) and sector (Software) from profile [P1, P2] Needs Validation: • Measurement basis of the 500M messages figure (total vs. per month) [C2, C3] • Independent corroboration of the $23.1M raised figure (per Pitch Deck Hunt) and its date [C1] • Revenue, burn rate, and cash position • Team composition and credentials • Problem statement and solution description • Market size and competitive landscape • Business model and monetisation mechanism • Use of proceeds • Product description • Risk factors Next evidence to supply: Audited or reviewed financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow) covering at least the most recent fiscal year, to establish revenue, burn, and cash position. Supported Points The company states 140,000+ bots on a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1], indicating meaningful platform adoption at that point in time, though the figure is self-reported and not independently verified. The company states a messages figure of either 500M total or 500M/month (measurement basis unresolved; see open concerns) on the same traction slide [S2, S3], suggesting material message volume on the platform at that time. Open Concerns Measurement-basis contradiction in the headline usage metric: the deck states '500M messages' without an interval on page 10 and '500M messages/month' on page 12 [C2, C3]. These are not necessarily the same figure; until management clarifies whether 500M is a cumulative total or a monthly rate, the scale of platform activity cannot be reliably interpreted. The $23.1M raised figure [C1, S4] is reported by Pitch Deck Hunt with no stated date and no independent evidence to establish or contradict it; the actual amount raised, when it was raised, and the resulting capital structure remain unknown. No revenue, burn, or cash data are present in the extracted evidence, making it impossible to assess financial sustainability, monetisation progress, or how long the company can operate without additional funding. No team, product, problem, market, or risk information was extracted from the document, representing the large majority of the standard due-diligence framework and leaving the investment thesis almost entirely unsubstantiated by the available evidence. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece of evidence is a set of financial statements — or at minimum a dated revenue and cash-burn schedule — that would establish whether ManyChat's stated usage scale (140,000+ bots, 500M messages [S1, S2, S3]) has translated into any monetisation, and how long the company can operate — from the dated cash and burn alone, since its reported funding is historical funding, not cash on hand [S4].
